facts.claim: Gold was found on Bendigo Creek in 1851, turning a sheep station into one of colonial Australia's largest boomtowns and drawing migrants from Europe and China.
The gold-rush wealth built grand Victorian public buildings in the city centre; Sacred Heart Cathedral is the third-largest cathedral in Australia.
Bendigo is about 140 km north-north-west of Melbourne (around 1.5 hours by car) and is Victoria's fourth-largest city.
Visitors can go underground at Central Deborah Gold Mine and ride the historic Bendigo tourist tramway, which offers a talking-tram tour.
Sun Loong, the world's longest imperial dragon, is shown in the Golden Dragon Museum outside the Easter Festival procession, reflecting the Chinese heritage of the goldfields.
Bendigo Art Gallery is one of Australia's oldest and largest regional galleries and sits beside Rosalind Park and the Poppet Head Lookout.

experiences: Go underground in a gold-rush mine
Ride a heritage tram through town

tips.title: Book for Easter
tips.detail: The Easter Festival procession draws tens of thousands over the long weekend, so book beds well ahead.

tips.title: Summer gets hot
tips.detail: Days above 35 C are common in summer and the record is 45.4 C. Plan mine and walking visits for morning.

tips.title: Ride the talking tram
tips.detail: The tourist tram links the Central Deborah mine and the Chinese heritage sites, so it works as a loop tour.

best_months.rationale: Mild autumn and spring days. January maxima average about 30 C with frequent 35 C+, and July minima fall to 3 C with most rain June to September.

wikivoyage_page: redirect https://en.wikivoyage.org/wiki/Greater_Geelong (Bellarine Peninsula redirects to Greater Geelong, which has a Bellarine Peninsula region section)

facts.claim: The Bellarine Peninsula lies south-west of Melbourne between Port Phillip, Corio Bay and Bass Strait, and with the Mornington Peninsula it separates Port Phillip Bay from Bass Strait.
About 70,000 people live there and the population roughly doubles at peak summer periods.
It became a holiday destination in the 1870s when Melbourne visitors arrived by paddle steamer to fish and swim; today it is known for beaches, seaside resorts, small towns and wineries.
Searoad Ferries has run a vehicle ferry from Queenscliff to Sorrento on the Mornington Peninsula since 1987.
The Bellarine Railway runs tourist services between Drysdale and Queenscliff, and the Bellarine Rail Trail runs alongside it.
Marine life seen around the peninsula includes southern right whales, Burrunan dolphins, Australian fur seals and sea lions.

experiences: Swim and surf at beach towns

tips.title: Cross by ferry
tips.detail: The Queenscliff to Sorrento ferry takes cars to the Mornington Peninsula and saves driving round the bay.

tips.title: Summer crowds
tips.detail: The population roughly doubles in peak summer, so book stays early and arrive at beaches before midday.

best_months.rationale: Summer is beach and holiday season; the population doubles at peak periods (shoulder months March and November are quieter).

facts.claim: Mansfield is a country town about two hours' drive north-east of Melbourne and the support town for Mount Buller ski resort.
Mount Buller has 22 lifts, the highest lift capacity in Victoria, with a top lifted point of 1780 m and about 300 hectares of skiable area.
Mount Stirling is a cross-country and backcountry ski area, and in summer hiking and mountain biking are popular on both mountains.
Lake Eildon is the only inland waterway in Victoria where houseboats are permitted, with over 700 on the lake.
Lakes Eildon and Nillahcootie are popular for waterskiing in summer.
Mansfield is on the Ned Kelly Trail; police killed by the Kelly gang at Stringybark Creek are buried in Mansfield Cemetery.
Craig's Hut, a high-country cattlemen's hut, is a Mansfield-region walk and tour destination.

experiences: Ski and snowboard at Mount Buller
Hike and bike the high country
Cruise and waterski on Lake Eildon

tips.title: Carry wheel chains
tips.detail: Wheel chains must be carried on the road up to Mount Buller throughout the winter season.

tips.title: Drive up from Melbourne
tips.detail: Mansfield is reached by car, about two hours via the Yarra Valley; allow extra time on winter weekends.

best_months.rationale: Two seasons: winter snow for Mount Buller and Stirling, and summer for lakes, hiking and mountain biking. Exact ski season dates unverified.

seasonal_tags: ski season (winter, southern hemisphere); summer lakes

facts.claim: The Dandenong Ranges are low mountain ranges about 35 km east of Melbourne, rising to 633 m at TV-tower-topped Mount Dandenong.
Puffing Billy, a heritage steam railway, runs 24 km on its original mountain track from Belgrave to Gembrook and is the most popular attraction in the ranges.
Sheltered gullies hold temperate rainforest, tree ferns and mountain ash forest, and wildlife includes superb lyrebirds and kookaburras.
The Kokoda Memorial Track (1000 Steps) is a steep 1.5 km staircase with historical plaques, and is busy on weekends.
The hill villages of Olinda, Sassafras and Kallista sit in the valley between the hills, with the Yarra Valley wineries just to the north.
The ranges have been a day-trip and weekend retreat for Melburnians since the 1870s.

experiences: Ride a steam train through the hills
Walk fern gullies and tall forest
Wander hill-village gardens and tea rooms
Look out over Melbourne from the summit

tips.title: Train from Melbourne
tips.detail: Belgrave line trains reach Belgrave in just over an hour, where Puffing Billy departs. Buses up the hills run rarely.

tips.title: Dress for the hills
tips.detail: Daytime temperatures run 4 to 6 C cooler than Melbourne's lower suburbs, and winter fog is common.

tips.title: Check fire restrictions
tips.detail: The ranges are bushfire-prone; summer fire restrictions apply, there is no camping in the national park and no rubbish bins.

best_months.rationale: Cooler, milder hill weather suits walking; summer carries fire restrictions and winter brings fog (4 to 6 C cooler than Melbourne). Autumn colour and spring garden timing unverified.
